theorems.description: For S₀, K, σ, T > 0 and k > −1, under a pricing measure where Z ~ N(0,1), the jump count N ~ Poisson(Λ) and the log-jump sizes Jᵢ ~ N(log(1+k) − δ²/2, δ²) are mutually independent (N of (Z, J), Z of J, the Jᵢ of each other), the jump-diffusion terminal price is S_T = S₀ exp((r − σ²/2)T − kΛ + σ√T·Z + ∑_{i<N} Jᵢ). import MathFin.BlackScholes.MertonModel

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory
open scoped NNReal

/-- **Merton's call formula, derived from the jump-diffusion.** The discounted expected call
payoff of `S_T = S₀ exp((r − σ²/2)T − kΛ + σ√T·Z + ∑_{i<N} Jᵢ)` is the Poisson mixture of
Black–Scholes prices `mertonCallPrice`. -/
theorem merton_call_formula_thm {Ω : Type*} [MeasurableSpace Ω] {Q : Measure Ω}
    [IsProbabilityMeasure Q] {S_0 K r σ T k δ : ℝ} {Λ : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ} {N : Ω → ℕ}
    {J : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (h : MathFin.MertonHyp Q k δ Λ Z N J) (hS_0 : 0 < S_0) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T) (hk : -1 < k) :
    ∫ ω, Real.exp (-r * T) * max (S_0 * Real.exp ((r - σ ^ 2 / 2) * T - k * Λ
        + σ * Real.sqrt T * Z ω + ∑ i ∈ Finset.range (N ω), J i ω) - K) 0 ∂Q
      = MathFin.mertonCallPrice S_0 K r σ T k δ Λ :=
  MathFin.merton_call_formula h hS_0 hK hσ hT hk

theorems.description: Let X be a jump-diffusion log-price process (as in mf-jump-diffusion-exponential-martingales) and S_t = S₀e^{X_t} with S₀ > 0. theorems.name: The Esscher Transform of a Jump-Diffusion Log-Return Law Is a Jump-Diffusion Law

The statement is about the law at one date, not about the process under a changed measure.

theorems.description: In the jump-diffusion model JumpDiffusionHyp Q Λ Z N J (Merton's independence structure with i.i.d. log-jump sizes J i of any law, the Poisson(Λ) jump count N independent of them; the library's Gaussian-jump MertonHyp is not an instance as stated), for a measurable set A of sizes with p = Q(J₀ ∈ A), the number of jumps with size in A is Poisson(p·Λ), the number with size in Aᶜ is Poisson((1 − p)·Λ), and the two counts are independent; for A = (0, ∞) these are the up-jumps and the remaining jumps (log-size ≤ 0). Stated at a fixed horizon, for the model's single jump count.

import MathFin.BlackScholes.JumpDiffusionThinning

open MeasureTheory ProbabilityTheory MathFin
open scoped NNReal

/-- In the Merton jump-diffusion model `JumpDiffusionHyp Q Λ Z N J`, the jumps whose size lies in
a measurable set `A` and those whose size lies in `Aᶜ` arrive as independent Poisson counts with
means `Λ·Q(J₀ ∈ A)` and `Λ·Q(J₀ ∉ A)`. Re-export of `MathFin.JumpDiffusionHyp.jumpCounts_split`. -/
theorem merton_jump_counts_split {Ω : Type*} {mΩ : MeasurableSpace Ω} {Q : Measure Ω}
    {Λ : ℝ≥0} {Z : Ω → ℝ} {N : Ω → ℕ} {J : ℕ → Ω → ℝ} (h : JumpDiffusionHyp Q Λ Z N J)
    {A : Set ℝ} (hA : MeasurableSet A) :
    Q.map (fun ω ↦ PoissonThinning.marksIn J A (N ω) ω)
        = poissonMeasure ((Q (J 0 ⁻¹' A)).toNNReal * Λ) ∧
      Q.map (fun ω ↦ PoissonThinning.marksIn J Aᶜ (N ω) ω)
        = poissonMeasure ((1 - (Q (J 0 ⁻¹' A)).toNNReal) * Λ) ∧
      IndepFun (fun ω ↦ PoissonThinning.marksIn J A (N ω) ω)
        (fun ω ↦ PoissonThinning.marksIn J Aᶜ (N ω) ω) Q :=
  h.jumpCounts_split hA
